comment: The story rules (docs/systems/story-ontology.md §7), evaluated by engine/story/StoryRules. check: the built-in check that implements it; critic: judged by the AI reading the subgraph.

rules.text: Every act has at least one scene; acts follow the template's order.
rules.message: Act {act} has no scenes.

rules.text: Every main-line scene is reachable from the first scene along next/branchesTo.
rules.message: Scene {scene} can't be reached from the first scene.

rules.text: Every branch reaches an ending or a convergence.
rules.message: Scene {scene} is a dead end: it leads to no ending.

rules.text: Every choice point option has consequences.
rules.message: Choice {choice} option '{option}' changes nothing.

rules.text: The climax is in the last 25% of the main line.
rules.message: The climax {scene} comes at {percent}% of the main line.

rules.text: Every kernel scene turns its value.
rules.message: Kernel scene {scene} doesn't turn its value (charge {charge} before and after).

rules.text: Every kernel event is caused or enabled by an earlier event, or is the inciting incident.
rules.message: Kernel event {event} has no cause.

rules.text: Every action in a kernel scene serves an agent's goal.
rules.message: Action {event} serves no goal of its agent.

rules.text: Every setup is paid off, or marked openEnded.
rules.message: Setup {node} is never paid off.

rules.text: Every conflict is resolved, or deliberately left open.
rules.message: Conflict {node} is never resolved.

rules.text: A character participates only while alive (unless a flashback or undead).
rules.message: {character} is dead but takes part in scene {scene}.

rules.text: A character is in one location per scene.
rules.message: {character} is in {count} places at scene {scene}.

rules.text: A character refers only to what it knows at that scene.
rules.message: {character} mentions '{about}' in scene {scene} before knowing it.

rules.text: A unique item has one possessor at a time.
rules.message: Unique item {item} has {count} possessors at scene {scene}.

rules.text: Relationship changes have a cause: a scene that presents the change.
rules.message: The relationship {subject} → {object} changes at {scene} with no scene showing why.

rules.text: Travel between consecutive scenes is possible by connections.
rules.message: {character} goes from {from} to {to} between scenes with no way there.

rules.text: Every narrative role the template requires is filled.
rules.message: No character fills the {role} role.

rules.text: Every major character has need, desire, motivation and an arc or a reason not to change.
rules.message: Major character {character} has no {missing}.

rules.text: Relationships are consistent both ways.
rules.message: {subject} is {type} of {object}, but {object} isn't {inverse} of {subject}.

rules.text: Names are unique and distinguishable.
rules.message: {a} and {b} have names that start alike.

rules.text: Every character with a gameplay role has what it needs.
rules.message: {character} is a {role} but has no {missing}.

rules.text: Every character placed in the world has an AI package or a reason to stand still.
rules.message: {character} has no AI package.

rules.text: Every main-line kernel scene in gameplay mode is advanced by a main-quest stage.
rules.message: Kernel gameplay scene {scene} is advanced by no main-quest stage.

rules.text: Every alias is fillable.
rules.message: Alias {alias} of {quest} has no fill.

rules.text: Each quest is completable: required characters are alive when needed.
rules.message: {quest} needs {character} at {scene}, but they're dead by then.

rules.text: A quest's giver has a motivation consistent with the quest's.
rules.message: {giver} gives {quest} ({motivation}) without that motivation.

rules.text: Quest levels follow the difficulty curve.
Rewards fit the economy.
A quest that kills a character doesn't break a later quest that needs them.
rules.message: {quest} needs {character}, who dies at {scene} first.

rules.text: Every location used by a scene exists, with a build type.
rules.message: Scene {scene} is set in {location}, which {problem}.

rules.text: Every location is reachable from the start location by connections.
rules.message: {location} can't be reached from the start.

rules.text: The parts a scene needs in a location are in its required parts.
rules.message: Scene {scene} needs a {part} in {location}, which doesn't list one.

rules.text: A location's mood agrees with the scenes set there.
